Other excerpts (bullets, 'Or are you', 'View network') do not clearly fit.

Mainly fires on the slot right after '=' where a computed numeric result is about to be written in arithmetic checks ('3 \times 67 = 201', '3(83) = 249'). Separately fires on 'Locked'/'locked' and a place-name fragment.

Fires at the start of contact/location numbers in web text: the space or first digits of a street address after a venue name or 'located at', and of a phone number after 'call ... at' / 'Phone:'. Occasional other number or end-of-prompt tokens.

No clear trigger. Scattered tokens in math reasoning and web text; a few are copula/predicate positions ('BOTH are positive', 'a, b are vertical asymptotes', '[are] music') but most (subscript 1, 'concealed', '<', 'Im', 'choose') are unrelated.

Fires in math reasoning on the 'to'/'be' of double-checking phrases, above all 'just to be absolutely sure' and 'to ensure clarity'/'let's be precise'. Weaker on related self-check phrasing ('Let's try to verify', 'a simpler way', 'Okay').

Fires on a '-s' (or '/s', '-S') token: a hyphen joined to the first letter s of the second part of a hyphenated compound ('not-very-good-s|ounding', 'Twitter-s|avvy', 'set-s|crew', 'pre-s|ell'); once '-l'. Moderate excerpts are unrelated low-level tokens.

In math reasoning, fires on the last token of an operand in a short symbolic relation that is being stated as a condition or fact ('$|A| = B$ implies', 'If $V = A$, then', '$g(x) = g(-x)$', '$B - A = D - C$'), typically a variable, closing brace or parenthesis just before the relation sign or closing '$'.

Fires on a modifier word in a compound nominal just before its head noun: 'personality traits', 'career opportunities', 'career levels', 'cell walls', 'time of need', 'two-page', 'higher order thinking', 'galactic sources'.

No single trigger. A weak tendency toward '=' or an opening quote/parenthesis right before a value is given ('rt = rotor', 'Name = "Pete"', '= (wz - 1', 'Text says: "'), mixed with newlines, 'OF', a URL fragment and other math tokens.
Loose group of positive or affirming words ('Classy', 'Classixx', 'best', 'really', 'Yes', 'true') mixed with unrelated tokens ('arch', 'TREES', 'Multip-lying', 'Tur', 'directory', 'solutions').

Fires on a token inside a phrase that repeats or parallels a just-preceding phrase: a second 'label("$y$", (' or 'dir(' call in Asymptote code, 'Personhood' reused, 'there are no minor ... Just as there are no minor', 'iim-ahmedabad, iim-bangalore,', 'Wait, $\sin(...)$. Wait, $\sin', 'So $S$ must be ... So $S$ must be'.

In math reasoning, fires on the token that begins or continues the next item in a series of parallel-structured terms: the next coordinate definition ('* $B='), the next polynomial term ('+ b^2', '- bx^2', '\frac{b}{4}'), the next label(...) call, 'A to C, B to'; also a restated answer template '$A(1+\sqrt{B})'.

Fires on the first sub-word fragment of an uncommon or proper word that is split into pieces: 'Pequ|od', 'Sec|underabad', 'equ|ine', 'Equ|iery', 'jou|sted', 'pec|uniary', 'Pan|vel', 'Hem|ant', 'Che|ques', 'past|ime'. A couple of moderate excerpts ('PO Box', 'love') fit less well.

Fires on the question mark that ends the question in a math problem statement, right before the answer-format instruction ('Express your answer as', 'Please reason step by step'). Weaker on other end-of-problem-statement positions (final period or '$', the opening <think> token).

Fires mainly on 'all' used as a predeterminer before 'the/that/this/your/its' + noun ('all that gear', 'all the unhappiness', 'all your print requirements'). Related weaker cases are a verb or preposition right before a determiner-led object, often '... information' ('obtain this information', 'privacy of your Personal Information', 'use such technical information').

Fires in arithmetic on the token just before the digits of a computed numeric result: the space after '=', '\approx', '\cdot' or '-' and the decimal point in '0.01'/'0.173'. Weaker on separators inside other quantities ('1/4 onion', the date '03/30') and recipe list commas.

Scattered word-initial fragments and names with no shared context: ' Ronald' (Reagan, McDonald, S.) three times, ' Bol' (Bolts, Bolivar) twice, ' that' twice, plus unrelated pieces such as 'utr', ' bere', ' Ars' and '|('. The moderate excerpts are unrelated again.

Forms of the verb 'take' (take, takes, taken), mostly in light-verb idioms such as 'take place', 'take effect', 'take care of', 'take on'. Weaker activations fall on other light or generic verbs (do, say, getting, going).

The modifier or determiner directly before a noun that names a class, tier or sector: 'this category', 'many different levels', 'bzip2 formats', 'more affordable side of the spectrum', 'B2B) space', 'this arena', 'right direction', 'other ... verticals'. Strongest on 'this' in 'fall into this category'.

No single trigger: assorted tokens in math reasoning, including a term or digit that starts or sits inside an expression (three before '+ \frac'), and the judgement words 'enough', 'impossible', 'possible', 'proceed'. The moderate excerpts are scattered punctuation and digits.

Several unrelated things: ' of' in the quoted phrase 'The combined weight of how many treeks', sentence-final punctuation after a math statement ('$.', '.') which dominates the moderate excerpts, and assorted web-text tokens (' with', ' on', ' category', ' Process', ' Data', a table separator).

The variable letter (x, y, t) that begins a polynomial term and is immediately followed by an exponent, as in '$x^2 - ...', '2x^4 + ...', 'root of $t^2 - ...'. Weaker cases are the variable in a linear term such as '3x+1'.

The token just before a number or date that opens the next entry in a sequence: the newline before a numbered list item ('7. Wishes') or a dated blog entry ('Monday, March'), the comma in 'Wait, 70 is in', the space or '(' before a date, and digits inside forum timestamps.
The word ' absolute' in 'absolute value' in math reasoning, and to a lesser degree ' eigen' in 'eigenvalue(s)'. Two moderate excerpts ('P(3) =', '3^4 =') do not fit.

The final token of a LaTeX math expression or term, at or just before the closing '$': a closing brace of \end{pmatrix} or \sqrt{6}, a closing parenthesis, the last digit or symbol of a polynomial, or the '$.' itself. One strong excerpt (' or' in 'factored or completed') does not fit.

Three unrelated triggers: the first sub-word of a term straight after an opening quotation mark ('"in-versely', '"gar-age', '"car-cinoid', '"con-secutive'); the comma that closes an introductory phrase in web prose ('Since 2000,', 'to generate a profit,'); and, at moderate level, the newline or indentation before a new bullet in math reasoning.

About half the strong excerpts are the '=' or space just before the result of a short arithmetic sum (digit sums such as '1+1+7=9', fraction sums), plus the space before a degree number. The rest, and all the moderate excerpts, are unrelated web tokens (' developed', '.sl', ' Labor', 'oo', ' bells', ' Easter').

Mainly the separator between items of a long enumeration: commas in keyword or place-name lists, newlines or dashes between list entries. A second, unrelated trigger is the number or space before a number in a duration phrase ('for six years', 'more than 20 minutes', 'about three months').

The line break, indentation or bullet marker that sits right before a line beginning 'Wait' in math reasoning, usually after a question or a check. Weaker related cases are line or item separators in web lists (newline between entries, comma in a synonym list, ');' ending a code line).

Unrelated tokens: ' past' or 'ast' in 'pastels' and 'pastoral' (three), ' raw' and ' Raw' (two), the '+' after '25x^2' in a repeated polynomial (two), and single cases such as ' Dante', 'R', 'epend'. The moderate excerpts share nothing with these.

No describable trigger. A few tokens recur (' seems' in 'This seems too simple' twice, ' As' twice, a digit before a divisibility bar twice), but the rest are unrelated words (' strong', 'med', ' keep', ' up', ' children', ' than', ' perfect').

Short function words in non-English text (Danish 'af', 'alle'; Portuguese 'todo', 'e'; French 'dans'), and English quantifier or particle words of the same kind (' all', ' half', ' up' in 'Set up'). The shared thread is quantifiers meaning 'all' and prepositions; moderate excerpts are looser (' of', ' throughout', ' said').

The dollar sign (or the token carrying it, such as ':$', ' ($') directly before a price, and a digit inside a dollar amount ('$1.05 billion'); one case is the space before a decimal after '\approx'. The moderate excerpts are mostly unrelated words (' seen', ' no', ' Airport', '\frac').

A digit or dash inside the second half of a numeric range or identifier in reference-style text: page ranges in citations ('2309-2318', '121-129'), confidence-interval ranges ('13.69-25.1'), year ranges, DOIs. Weaker cases are prices in several currencies and other bare numbers.

' San' in place names, mostly after 'University of' (San Francisco, San Diego, San Quintin) accounts for four strong excerpts. The others are unrelated: digits opening a parenthesised difference in math, and words such as ' Content', ' Teacher', ' directed', 'cont'; moderate excerpts are unrelated too.

In math reasoning, ' make' in 'that doesn't make sense' and ' no' in 'that makes no sense', where the model rejects an interpretation it has just considered. None of the moderate excerpts (digits, ' to', ' case') fit.

No describable trigger: tokens include ' vs', ' to', ',', ' via', ' Class', digits in arithmetic, '\sqrt', '.', ' let', ' am'. Several strong excerpts lie near the start of a document, but the marked tokens have nothing in common.

A token inside a math expression that is being copied out again: the problem's expression re-quoted from the prompt ('Let's check the prompt again. "If $|x+5|...'), or a calculation or statement written a second time after 'Wait'. Activation falls part-way through the restated expression.

Two unrelated triggers: ' opt' or 'Opt' as the start of 'opt-in', 'Optical', 'optogenetics' (four strong), and forms of the verb 'give' ('will give', 'gives no indication') (four strong, one moderate). A few other tokens ('ing', ' flag', ' clear', ' Class', ' term') fit neither.

The verb or preposition that links a creative work to its themes in a synopsis or review ('drama explores', 'works deal with', 'tale of', 'story about'), and the commas inside the list of themes that follows ('isolation, fear of the unknown,').
Words expressing that something persists or is ongoing: ' still', ' continue' and 'continues to', 'persisting', 'lingered with me', ' lingering'.

In math reasoning, the '=' or the space after '=' that comes right before the computed result of a short arithmetic evaluation, typically when substituting a value or checking ('2+4+2=8', '... + 1 = 3.5'). Moderate excerpts are mostly digits inside numbers or expressions and fit only loosely.

The token immediately before the word 'the' (or 'The'): a verb, preposition, comma or bullet after which the definite article comes next ('satisfies the', 'with the', 'on the', ', the'). In a few cases the following word is not 'the' ('Chum is', '! She').

The token just before, or at the start of, the numeric value of a trigonometric or complex-exponential evaluation: the '=' or '\approx' space or the decimal point in 'cos 53 \approx 0.6018', 'e^{i\pi/3} = 1/2 + ...', '(cos 60, sin 60) = (0.5, ...'.

Mostly the last digit of an angle measure directly before '^\circ' in geometry reasoning (90, 180, 360 degrees), plus mid-word pieces of geometry terms ('isosceles', 'parallelogram'). A separate trigger is the prime in a derivative 'f'(x)', 'g'(x)'; moderate excerpts are unrelated.

A pause point inside a sentence of informal, often first-person web prose, right before the sentence carries on with a further clause: mostly a comma ('however, that', 'my family, to focus'), sometimes a pronoun or adverb before 'that' or a continuation ('acknowledged to me that', 'and also in part'). The moderate excerpts fit only loosely.

Words for still bodies of water, chiefly 'lake' / 'Lake' / 'lakes' (including in place names such as Lake Michigan, Lake Placid), also 'pond', and 'reflections' or 'water' in descriptions of water scenery.

Pronouns, auxiliaries and other function words inside Bible quotations and prayer language ('If you then, though you were evil', 'on earth as it is in heaven', 'then I will hear from heaven', 'thine hands'). The trigger is the scriptural register, not a particular token.

A determiner or possessive pronoun (their, our, your, the, its many) that opens the object noun phrase right after a verb or preposition, most strongly after 'forgive' / 'forget (about)' / 'keep' in religious or reflective prose. The moderate excerpts are mostly weak, unrelated firings on digits inside math expressions.

In math reasoning, fires on a token inside the second of two parallel statements that reuses the template of the one just before it ("$x$ is not a multiple of 5. $y$ is", "Second term", "consecutive even ... consecutive odd integers", "6_8 ... 7_8", "5 upper class ... 10 lower class"). Moderate excerpts are weak firings on assorted digits and symbols in formulas without a visible parallel.

Loosely: a noun naming someone's life circumstances (life, lives, marriage, professional affairs, event) that is the object of a 'make X better/difficult' construction or the subject about to receive a predicate; also the verb 'making/turning' in similar self-help contexts. Several excerpts (team, school history, literacy, subtract) fit only weakly.

Mostly math: the last token of an expression just before '\implies' / '\Rightarrow' (e.g. 'x=0 \implies'), or the final term inside a parenthesised factor before the closing bracket ('(1-x))', '(n+1)}'). Separately it fires in prose on a pronoun/determiner after a fronted phrase ('In the back of her mind she', 'from her bag', 'download this').

The word 'emotions' (and 'emotional'), especially as the head noun in phrases about feeling or expressing emotions. Weaker firings occur on neighbouring words in feeling/emotion contexts (felt, arousal, 'emotionally and').

The first token of a proper name or named title as it begins (Heaney, PR Newswire, Rose Pak, Belichick, San Bernardino, Ace Ventura, Guy, 'Die lustigen Weiber'), often right after a sentence boundary or a preposition; a quoted phrase opening ('"Two-thirds') and 'crèche' are looser variants. The moderate excerpts (bullets, digits, 'but', newline) do not fit.

The first sub-word fragment of a multi-token verb, usually Latinate, before its suffix is completed: preced|e, outper|forms, disqual|ify, incentiv|izing, persu|ading, perme|ated, encaps|ulates, encompass|es. Weaker firings on similar split stems (adm|iring, herald|ed, re-e|valuate, \per|p).

A relational word that links a preceding noun/verb to the complement about to follow in expository prose: governed prepositions ('outside of', 'depends on', 'snapshot of', 'infringes on', '52% of', 'tailor ... to') and transitive effect verbs ('improve', 'impact', 'increase', 'reduce') just before their object.

The verb 'keep' (keep your party together, keep in mind, keep playing, need to keep up), in imperative or infinitive use. All ten strong excerpts are this token; the moderate excerpts are unrelated weak firings, mostly on digits and symbols inside math expressions.

Specific word-initial sub-word fragments: 'acet'/'Ac'(et) in chemical names (acetone, acetate, acetaminophen), 'Hel' at the start of surnames (Helbig, Helu, Helmut), and 'Stere' in stereo- words; also 'Post Hoc', a drug-name fragment, 'hem', and a decimal digit. These are distinct token identities without a shared meaning.

Motion verbs of arriving at or encountering something: 'come to / come across / came to / came across' and 'converging'. It also fires strongly on unrelated math-formatting tokens (the closing ')$' of a point, the backslash before '\pmod' / '\equiv'), and moderately on assorted other words.
The word 'visual' in any casing or form (Visual Studio, Visual Novel, visual snow, visualise, visually, visuals, Chinese 视觉), with a weak firing on 'visible'.

In descriptive/informational text listing the characteristics of a thing, fires on the function word that attaches or continues a property: 'They have', 'an area with', 'a place with', 'chassis with', 'allows for', 'and are able', and the commas/'or'/'and' joining listed attributes.

A non-standard or mis-encoded apostrophe glyph plus the clitic that follows it in possessives and contractions (‘s, ´s, `s, ?s, ís, `t), i.e. where a plain ' would be expected. Related weaker firings on unusual dash glyphs joining clauses (―, ––, --) and on an ordinary 'd.

A token consisting of the letter D/d at the start of a word that is completed by following tokens (D|TS, D|olby, D|uma, D|istant, d|ementia, off-d|ry, guitar-d|renched). It also fires at similar strength on the copula in math/formal statements ('67 is a prime', 'should be made'), and the moderate excerpts are unrelated.

The first token of the head noun or name that follows a quantifier or determiner ('how many OSC|ars', 'these Toyota Si|enna', 'two Tre|os', 'three U.S.', 'how many such paralle|lograms', 'some Anna Nicole', 'All Kle|pper'), usually a rare multi-token word; 'with broken hips' / 'other big guys' are looser cases.

A summarising noun after a demonstrative that refers back to what was just said and becomes the subject of the next clause ('this freedom', 'these rankings', 'This amount', 'These goals', 'These coordinates', 'These numbers', 'a term which'), often re-using the earlier word. Related: the comma that closes a long subject/appositive just before its predicate.

An auxiliary or linking word just before a passive participle or an obligation/ability predicate: 'we are restricted', 'Martin was killed', 'was recently sentenced', 'you are required', 'may be taken', 'may be able', 'you're limited', 'have to', 'attempted to'. Moderate excerpts are weaker and only partly fit (will not be required, conspiracy to).

The first token of text that breaks abruptly from the preceding sentence: injected spam keywords ('Native dating Gateshead', 'hoodia'), web boilerplate ('Read More', 'Continue Reading', 'Anonymous said', 'Existing User', 'Kindly mention'), or a new label ('Calculation:', 'Result'). A few excerpts (golfers, the man, condition) are ordinary nouns that do not fit.

Two jobs with a loose 'what follows the equals/copula' theme: the first digit of a computed result right after '=' or '\times' in arithmetic (= 6468, = 53, 7 \times 53), and the predicate complement right after a copula in prose (It's ok, become impossible, the natural thing, are sisters, 'normal and reasonable'). Moderate excerpts mostly do not fit.

The connective or separator joining two parallel items when the second repeats the form of the first: 'and' / 'And' / 'then' / 'while' between parallel phrases ('one foot from the ceiling and one foot from', 'saddle covers and saddle bags', equation 'and' equation), plus the 'of' or ');' at the matching point of a repeated line. Moderate excerpts are weaker and mostly formula-internal tokens.

Two distinct triggers: a mid-word fragment inside a misspelled, garbled or letter-elongated word (annnnd, oppoortunity, committment, actitivies, WAAAAARRR, ooooo, multifl0w), and the first minutes digit after the colon in a clock time (6:35, 4:00) or a similar digit in a figure (£375m).

Most often the last character of a math expression just before its closing '$' or bracket (-18$, {6}$, = 1$, x+2)$, 274i$). The rest are unrelated: fragments of abbreviations/long words (D-M|ich, O|tor|rino, n|esc|is), line indentation and line breaks between reasoning steps, and 'Let'.

Metalinguistic contexts about which word or wording was used: the token leading into a cited term, as in 'never use that word', 'did not notice the "mini"', 'did not use the terrorism word', 'the prompt uses the term', 'is labeled XT2', 'titled CPC', and in math reasoning 'No, it explicitly says "even"' / 'specifically asks for'.

Text about standardized tests and competitions as the source or type of a question: the preposition/connective leading into the source ('found in math competitions like AMC', 'appear in standardized tests', 'a problem from a math competition', 'This looks like a typical puzzle'), and test-section labels (SAT Math, SAT Verbal, Section 3, non verbal).

In math reasoning, the indentation whitespace that starts a new line right after a line stating an equation (typically '... = 0'), i.e. where the next solving step (Roots:, Factor:, x = ...) is about to begin. A few other tokens ('$' opening an equation, 'the', '\ge') fire too, and the moderate excerpts are unrelated weak firings.

Commas (or equivalent separators) between items in a list of software products, file formats or brand names: 'EndNote, ProCite, RefMan', 'Avi, Divx, Xvid', 'OGG, WAV', 'Internet Explorer, Mozilla Firefox, Google Chrome', 'Visa, MasterCard', Wikimedia project names.

Several unrelated token triggers: the verb 'come' in 'come to / come into' (come to an end, come into its own), the possessive 'its' after 'as/to', a hyphen plus 'c' starting a hyphenated word (Off-C|ampus, pre-c|andidate, EV-c|ertificate), plus 'makes' and 'those'. Moderate excerpts are unrelated.

Mainly the sub-word 'Gro'/'gro' at the start of a name or word (Grohl, Grobbelaar, Grover, Groovy, grooves, ground-breaking). It also fires on the minus sign / following space in arithmetic ('4100 - 3200', '= -55') and on a few other word starts (clean, trans|istors).

The token right before the next member of a predictable series or fixed pair: 'Part' before XIII after Part XII, a list bullet/newline before 'Wednesday' after Tuesday, the space or '=' before the next number in an incrementing list or enumeration of cases (..., 126, 133; y=12 then y=13; 7x22 then 7x23), and 'and' in 'pros and cons'.

No describable trigger: the marked tokens are scattered (' of', ' sub', ' limit', '/', ' over', ' sw', '-L', digits) across math reasoning and web text. The only weak cluster is tokens adjacent to a '\neq' check in three math excerpts.

Closing bracket tokens in LaTeX math that end a parenthesised or braced group right before a following parallel group, e.g. ')}' or '}}' closing the numerator of a \frac or a \sqrt argument, or '),' between listed terms. Moderate excerpts are other math delimiters and openers (\frac, '|', '$', ' (') rather than closers.

Mixture: the decimal point or space/equals right before a numeric result in math ('\approx 0[.]04', '= [ ]2520'), the words ' optional'/' optical' in web text, and assorted mid-phrase function words (' in' use, ' aimed' at, used ' to'). No shared trigger is evident.

Two triggers: a comma late in a long enumeration of place names or letters (US states, countries, set elements such as {B, G, O[,] R, V}), and the token ' Hob' in Hoboken / Hobbit. Moderate excerpts are unrelated tokens in math reasoning.

The token 'fact'/'Fact'/'Factor' (factoring out, Fact or Fiction, the fact that) accounts for four strong excerpts; the remainder are unrelated tokens such as list commas, digits inside numbers, a newline, ' built', ' relation'.

Fires inside the second or later instance of a parallel or repeated construction, at the point where the text re-uses an earlier template: 'the value of X controls ... the value of [Y]', 'a lesson to us all ..., and [a] lesson to me', 'today I celebrate ..., today I celebrate', repeated 'Photo credits:' and 'Premium Content Part' entries, 'Decide to place ... Decide [to] place'. Moderate excerpts are mostly digits in dates and unrelated words.
Mainly the token ' Star' in 'Star Trek' / 'Starfleet' (six of ten strong excerpts). The other strong and all moderate excerpts are unrelated tokens (' simplest', ' or', ' Place', ' dwarf', ' North').

Tokens that join or introduce the second member of a pair of alternatives or contrasted items: ' or' in 'Day or night', 'Fact or Fiction', 'the person, or the action', 'vs [roman]', 'Republican legislatures and [Democratic] governors', 'as [important] as'. Other excerpts (newlines between list entries, math variables) do not fit.

Tokens in the first few positions of an algebraic equation or expression that is being written out during a check or substitution step in math reasoning, typically coefficients, parentheses around a plugged-in value, or operators ('5(2[)] + 4(-3', '[|]5(-1)-', 'Substitute k=1 back: [ (]3^1)').

A noun or adjective acting as the modifier in a compound noun phrase, just before the head noun, usually naming a domain or product category: 'property [tax] breaks', '[Camera] Features', 'Dairy [Processor] Grant', 'user [object] searches', 'block [cheese] price', '[student] activism'.

In math reasoning, tokens inside power and root expressions: the base 2 or the caret when a number is rewritten as a power of 2 ('64 = [2]^6', '2[^]8', '\sqrt[8]{[2]^5}'), and the backslash starting '\pm' or '\times' in a root or exponent expression. A chat-template token, a table brace and all moderate excerpts do not fit.

The LaTeX token 'sqrt' in root expressions, especially nth roots like '\sqrt[8]{', covers three strong and one moderate excerpt. The rest are unrelated tokens (' $', 'AB', ' office', a bullet, ' there', ' to', ' speak', ' optimization').

Object pronoun ' it' / ' them' directly after an action verb ('do it', 'read it again', 'started it', 'ordering them'), with a related offshoot on general process verbs after a subject describing how things proceed ('not everything [goes]', 'time can [go]', 'they [happen]', 'toys [come]', 'just [acting]').

No single trigger. Small clusters only: ' $' introducing a price after a comma in product listings (two excerpts) and ' I' right after a closing quotation (two excerpts); the rest are assorted nouns and tokens (' trees', ' remote', ' clean', ' road', ' We').

The subject (or its verb) of a short clause that asserts or denies existence or occurrence after a conjunction such as if/or/but/since: mostly existential ' there' in 'if there is', 'OR there isn't', 'if indeed there was', plus 'but [I] don't', 'Sure [he] did', 'since she [took] one'. Some moderate excerpts are the second half of a 'one ... and one ...' pairing.

Tokens in math reasoning about trigonometric quantities, most often the position just before a value or expression is stated ('\cos 81 \approx[ ]0.15', '\cos(90) [=] 0', 'the relation [$\]sin x'). Token identity varies and several excerpts (base conversion, isolating x) are non-trig math steps.

Words in phrases stating the amount or level of something, especially nutritional content: 'high [in] Omega 3', 'low [in] calories', 'low-fat', 'increase [in] area', 'reduces the amount [of]', 'small [constant] overhead', 'Most of the fiber [and]'. Moderate excerpts drift to food ingredient lists and unrelated tokens.

Two triggers: LaTeX operator command names after a backslash in math, chiefly 'to' in limits ('x \[to] \infty') plus '\approx', '\cdot', '\sum'; and the word-piece ' sur' ('surging', 'surfer'). 'DEPENDS' and a few digits/spaces do not fit.

The token immediately preceding 'without', most strongly ' or' / ' and' in 'with or without', also 'bodyboard without', 'days without', 'those without'. A few weaker excerpts are nearby conditional phrasing ('even if you don't', 'would be complete without').

Two unrelated triggers: the word ' International' at the start of an organisation name (International Olympic Committee, Space Station, Lions Club, Choir), and ' $(' or closing parentheses opening/closing a coordinate tuple or bracketed expression in math reasoning.

Two unrelated triggers: the middle word of a fixed paired idiom, chiefly ' and' in 'tried and true/tested' (also 'first come, [first]-served', 'plug [and] play', 'step by [step]'), and the word 'Here' opening the model's reasoning right after the <think> tag.

Clauses that refer back to something done earlier, mostly the model questioning or flagging its own earlier step in math reasoning ('why did I write ...', 'I got the signs [wrong] before', 'As [calculated] before', 'Where did 2/15 come [from]?'), plus web text 'had not been [doing] previously'. Moderate web excerpts (' me', ',') mostly do not fit.

In math reasoning, the word that introduces a doubt, caveat or second look: 'Wait', 'One tiny [detail]', 'a potential [issue]', 'is there a [chance]', 'maybe the question is from a [context] where', 'anything [subtle]'.

Points where the model's reasoning quotes or restates wording from the problem statement or code: the opening quote mark or backtick ('Then ["]redistribute', 'The code says [`]return'), or a token inside the restated text (a comma in the restated colour list, the closing '$' of a quoted formula). A few web-text excerpts (' of' in 'one count of', ' given') and the moderate excerpts do not fit.
In math, the token immediately before a negative number, usually one in parentheses: '10 [-] (-16)', '1(1) + [1](-1)', '[+] (-5)(1)', '4[*](-2)', '7[,] -11', '\[cdot] (-2)'.

Loose cluster of words that precede an 'if'/'who'/conditional clause or sit in a hedged verb phrase ('hard to [tell] if', '[Only] if', 'love [it] if', '[even] if', 'what they [do]', 'might [do]'), mixed with unrelated tokens (' labor', ' hiring', a decimal point) and unrelated moderate excerpts.

Mixture: the space token before a multi-digit number in math ('- [ ]176y', '= [ ]1125', '+ [ ]1152'), the '-s' token starting the second half of a hyphenated compound ('no-squeezing', 'teacher-scholar', 'dog-sitting'), and unrelated words (' Local', ' change', ' and').

Mainly the word ' all' / ' All' in idiomatic uses ('you're all set', 'all about', 'all around us', 'All over the planet', 'All in all', 'all importantly'). The other three strong excerpts and all moderate excerpts are unrelated tokens.

Mainly the contraction token ''re' / ''s' directly after a subject pronoun or relative 'that' ('they're', 'He's', 'who're', 'that's') in web prose. A degree sign, a colon and all moderate excerpts (parentheses, commas, indentation in math) are unrelated.

In math reasoning, the demonstrative or verb in a sentence that passes judgment on the result just written: 'This [seems] correct/wrong', 'this [is] incorrect', '$...$ [is] wrong because', 'No, [that]'s wrong', 'No, [this] doesn't help'.
Unrelated triggers: the word ' link' / ' links', the token ' pop' / ' Pop' ('pop.', 'poplars', 'Popick'), and number words ' Two' / ' three'. Moderate excerpts are unrelated digits and LaTeX braces.

Two unrelated triggers: the stem ' wouldn' / ' couldn' before ''t' (also ' cannot'), and a hyphen, dash or plus joining numbers or a numeric prefix ('multi[-]tenant', '5[-]1/4', '7 [-] 13 kg', '360 [+] 36').

Fires inside phrases that name a relation or ratio between two things, on the second term or the word just before the relation noun: 'X-to-Y ratio' (performance-to-cost, buck-to-doe, employment-population, debt-income), 'relationship/link/distinction/gap between', 'hybrid of the two'.

In math reasoning and code, fires on the final token of a numeric item (last digit, closing bracket, or the line break after it) in a list or sequence of values/terms, just before the separator (comma, +, $, newline).
Fires on the word-initial fragment 'Ca'/'ca' (sometimes bare 'C') inside longer words, mostly foreign or proper names (Caleta, Icahn, Lescaut, Caen, Castronovo, Caumont, Caerwent, caiman, caulk).

Fires on the first token of a term or expression that already appeared earlier in the context and is now being restated: the opening fragment of a recurring unusual word (goolee, battalions, Asymptote) or the '$' / '*' that opens a repeated amount or expression. A few strong hits (list comma, coordinate minus, ATTENTION) do not fit.

In step-by-step math reasoning, fires at the start of the next line after an equation line: the bullet marker ' *' (or the newline/indent/list number) that begins the next step in a run of algebra steps. A few hits are tokens inside LaTeX expressions instead.

Two unrelated triggers: the division slash '/' in fractions or divisions (1/4, 729 / 9, 8/10), and function words in fixed idioms such as 'when it comes to' and 'at risk'. Moderate examples are scattered math tokens that fit neither.

Fires in technical text about radiation, detectors, medical imaging and therapy (brachytherapy dose, x-rays, count rates, CT detectors), on modifiers and function words just before a technical noun. Weaker activations are in other medical/dental/bioanalysis text.

Two unrelated triggers: tokens in the middle of arithmetic (a digit inside a computed number, or '=' / '(' just before a numeric result), and words about searching or hiding ('searching for', 'hiding'). One hit ('flag pole') fits neither.

Fires on the subject noun or the auxiliary/copula just before a predicate saying something is harmed, lost, exposed or at risk ('properties will be at risk', 'information stolen', 'was lost', 'would be vulnerable', 'are without electricity', 'were down'). Weaker hits are generic auxiliaries before other predicates.

Fires on ' a' used as 'per' in rate expressions: 'times a day', 'days a week', 'days a year', '$113,000 a year', '300 a week'. Weak activations occur on other tokens before time-unit words or on hyphens in math.

In math reasoning, fires on tokens inside text that restates or re-quotes something already written: quoted problem-statement sentences and 'Wait, ...' lines that repeat the preceding statement nearly verbatim (also 'Asymptote' and 'Tassels' repeated shortly after first mention).

Fires inside ALL-CAPS text, on a token that continues a capitalised word or headline (L|EMON, C|RAWLING, TE|ETH, DUST OR). Weaker hits are other mid-unit continuations: a line break in the middle of a hard-wrapped sentence, or a hyphen/slash joining compound words.

Fires in the opening restatement of a math problem at the start of the model's reasoning ('The user wants me to compute...', 'Identify the operation: ...', 'Understand the Goal'), mostly on the quantity tokens of the described task. Moderate examples are scattered math tokens later in the reasoning.

Fires in financial/commercial text about benefits, offers, credits, fees and penalties, on the benefit/fee word or the preposition after it ('benefits to', 'benefit of', 'offer to extend credit', 'fees for', 'penalized for').

Fires inside calendar-date expressions: the preposition before a date ('celebrated on November 9', 'last Monday in May', 'evening of November 9', 'through Easter Sunday') and the day-number digit just before a month name ('8 June', '16 October').

Two unrelated triggers: the math-mode opener at the start of an expression ('$$' on a new indented line of display math; weaker on inline ' $' after 'So'/'Since'), and the token ' pop' (populating, pop., popups). '\hline' and ' fact' fit neither.

Fires on the subject (or the word right after it) of a clause about things fitting or working out as a whole: 'all the pieces fell into place', 'how the pieces fit together', 'it all came together', 'check if the numbers add up / match'. Weaker on 'it all' + seems/feels.

Most strong hits are on 'open' or inside words beginning with O (O|reg|ano, Olive Garden, O|zz|ie, Oatmeal), but others are a line-initial capital 'S' starting a title and unrelated words; moderate examples show no shared trigger.

In math reasoning, fires near the end of an expression that is being copied verbatim from the problem statement or code (after 'Prompt:', 'the user wrote:', 'the code draws', 'input string', 'Output:'), typically on the last digit before a closing delimiter. Weaker on equations restated after 'Wait,'.

In math reasoning, fires on the token immediately before a fraction value is written, usually '=' (also '(-', '^{', '}') followed by something like 1/4, 5/12, 1/2, 3/2. A few hits and most moderate examples do not fit.

Fires on the word 'spider' / 'Spider' (Spider-Man, a spider), with related firing on 'Sp|itzer' and on a few other name tokens in pop-culture contexts (Krysten Ritter, Jonas Brother, Lady luck). Moderate examples are unrelated.

Fires in phrases about acquiring a skill: 'learn to drive', 'learning how to use', 'skills to be learned', 'learn another language', 'demonstrate competence', 'get the hang of it', 'practice in that art'.
Fires on a collective, quantity or kind noun that is immediately followed by 'of': 'a set of', 'years of', 'a pool of', 'a matter of', 'habit of', 'type of', 'amounts of', 'a group of'.

Two unrelated triggers: Bible citations and biblical text (book names such as '2 Chronicles', 'Proverbs', 'Abraham, Isaac and Jacob'), and the decimal point in radio frequencies ('2.4 GHz', '9.375 GHz', '2.402').

In math text, fires on the variable or symbol right after an opening '$' when a single named quantity is being referred to ('coefficient of $x$', 'Then $x = ...', 'Old $P = ...', 'the $t$ coefficient'). Weaker on the first token of other math expressions and on product model identifiers (XT, iPhone 6).

Fires on the token immediately before the word 'no' in negative-quantity phrases: 'little or no', 'few or no', 'accepts no liability', 'there is/are no', 'makes no sense'. Weaker on similar slots before 'zero' or an empty-ish set.

Fires in statements of a ratio, fraction or proportion, on the token just before the ratio's value or terms are given ('the ratio A : B : C =', 'in ratio 2:1', 'ratios from 19.2/...', 'the fraction is 2/3', 'ratio of good is to bad').
No clear trigger. A few hits are the object pronoun ' it' ('Got it back', 'directed it to be abandoned', 'bring it into'), but the rest are unrelated digits, nouns and conjunctions.

Fires at the end of a just-named entity or noun phrase, on the punctuation or first word that follows it and starts the continuation ('Amanda -', '$n$,', 'the set of 6,', "'D' small cities", 'Stephanie Gross spends'). The pattern is loose and positional.

In narrative prose about people, fires on the word right before an action verb following a just-mentioned person: infinitive 'to' ('asked my husband to mail', 'reached over to turn'), an auxiliary, or a subject pronoun ('once she realized', 'but he just stopped'). Moderate hits in math text do not fit.

Math-reasoning tokens with two loosely separate triggers: the start of the second operand in a difference or pair inside parentheses (vector components '(4 - 0', gcd arguments, 'x_2' after 'x_1'), and ' the' in re-quoted fixed phrases ('turn to the right', 'What is the distance', 'volume and surface area').

Fires on the second (or a later) digit of a multi-digit number, right after its first digit(s), mostly in prose: dates (July 27, August 17), counts (247 million, about 15 officers), percentages (47%), ordinals (14th, 44th).

Fires in phrases about spending time on an activity: the tokens 'spend/spent' and the time-span noun that follows ('hours', 'afternoon', 'a day'), plus nearby leisure-time phrasing ('after school and on the weekends', 'the day off to', 'in my spare time, I').
